minutes.headline: Assessors held the revaluation disclosure period open, drafted a card-reading guide, and wanted more data on senior exemptions.
minutes.summary: The board discussed the revaluation rollout: the disclosure period, resident questions on lakefront ratings and qualified sales, and a draft guide to reading the property card. A long debate covered the senior orientation agenda and a proposal to change the Clause 41C senior exemption age and amount, which members said needs better cost data before town meeting. The board voted on the senior tax work-off payout, signed invoices and a motor vehicle excise commitment, and set the next meeting for March 4.

attendees.role: member of the public on Zoom

public_comment.topic: Resident raised the impact statement sent to second-home owners, missing Vision property cards on the website, and which sale years were used for lake properties.
Resident asked for the criteria Vision used to validate lakefront ratings and how adjustment factors were calculated for average and below average with so few qualified sales.
Resident on Zoom thanked staff, said the table microphone is hard to hear, and asked about a neighborhood map; told the GIS map covers the whole town.

votes.motion: Approve the senior property tax work-off payout for last year.
Sign motor vehicle excise commitment number seven for 2023 (discussed whether a motion was needed).
Motion to adjourn (heard as 'motion to a... second').

budget_items.what_was_said: An invoice from Vision was signed as part of the agreed contract; no vote taken.
The MFS bill covered hours of calls, emails and work on the DOR submission and classification hearing presentation.
The total payout for roughly eleven participants for the prior year was put to a vote.
A late-year commitment of bills for 135 vehicles was signed.
Members debated the cost to the town of raising the exemption and lowering the age, with state reimbursement and per-person amounts disputed.
Members discussed spreading the cost over parcels as a few dollars per household.

decisions.decision: The disclosure period will be extended by a day to end the following Tuesday.
The office will ask Vision for the original property cards and field comments on the 12 qualified sales.
The line about the assessment date was to be deleted from the how-to-read guide.
The senior center orientation will be cut to four items, dropping the circuit breaker and revaluation material.
The Wednesday meeting was not posted; the next meeting is March 4, with a joint meeting with the select board March 12 and March 18 after.
The 41C proposal will be reworked with better data before the board takes a position.

what_happened.line: The Assessors extended the revaluation disclosure period by a day, to end the following Tuesday.
The board will ask Vision for the original property cards and field comments on the qualified sales that residents questioned.
The board cut the senior center orientation to four items, dropping the circuit breaker and revaluation material.
No position was taken on a Clause 41C senior exemption change; the proposal goes back to be reworked with better cost data.
The board signed a motor vehicle excise commitment and put the senior tax work-off payout to a vote; the vote outcomes were not audible.

why_it_matters: The revaluation sets how homes, including lakefront and second homes, are rated, and residents questioned how those ratings were validated from so few qualified sales.
A change to the 41C senior exemption would shift cost onto other taxpayers, and the board has said it needs better cost data before town meeting, where residents may be asked to vote on it.
watch_next: Next Assessors meeting on March 4, then a joint meeting with the Select Board on March 12.
The reworked Clause 41C proposal and the Vision property cards and field comments on the qualified sales.
